title: Copán dynasty founded
description: The foreign lord Yax K'uk' Mo' is installed as king of Copán, founding the dynasty that builds the great Maya city.

title: Columbus at the Bay Islands
description: On his fourth voyage Columbus meets a Maya trading canoe off Guanaja and weeks later lands near modern Trujillo, the first European contact in Honduras.

title: Trujillo founded
description: Hernán Cortés marches overland from Mexico and orders the founding of Trujillo, the colony's main Caribbean port.

title: San Pedro Sula founded
description: Pedro de Alvarado founds the town that grows into the industrial capital.

title: Lempira's revolt defeated
description: Spanish captains put down the Lenca rising led by the chief Lempira, who is killed; his name later marks the national currency.

title: English destroy Trujillo
description: An English expedition sacks and burns the colony's main Caribbean port, a blow from which the town never fully recovers.

title: San Fernando de Omoa fortress
description: Spain builds the largest fortress in Central America to guard the coast against pirates and the British.

title: Garífuna arrive at Roatán
description: Britain deports some five thousand Garífuna from Saint Vincent to Roatán, and they spread along the mainland coast.

title: First head of state
description: Dionisio de Herrera takes office as the first elected head of the state of Honduras and gives it its first constitution.

title: Independence
description: Honduras breaks away from the Federal Republic of Central America and becomes a sovereign state.

title: National university founded
description: President Juan Lindo founds the society that becomes the National Autonomous University of Honduras.

title: William Walker executed
description: The American filibuster who ruled Nicaragua is handed over by the British navy, tried and shot at Trujillo.

title: Capital moved to Tegucigalpa
description: President Marco Aurelio Soto transfers the seat of government from Comayagua to booming Tegucigalpa.

title: Banana companies arrive
description: New Orleans fruit merchants set up on the north coast, the start of the company era that dominates the country's politics.

title: ‘Banana republic’ coined
description: In a book of stories O. Henry coins the term ‘banana republic’, modelled on the Honduras he knew.

title: Carías takes office
description: General Tiburcio Carías Andino becomes president and holds power for sixteen years, the longest rule in national history.

title: Great General Strike
description: Tens of thousands of banana workers strike for months and win contracts, the founding act of the Labour movement.

title: Villeda overthrown
description: A coup ends the reforming government of Ramón Villeda Morales and brings back military rule.

title: Football War
description: El Salvador attacks Honduras after riots at football matches between them; the four-day war kills thousands and ends with many Salvadoran settlers expelled.

title: Hurricane Fifi
description: Hurricane Fifi floods the north-coast valleys and kills around eight thousand people, mostly in banana country.

title: Civilian rule restored
description: Roberto Suazo Córdova takes office as the first civilian president in nearly a decade, though the army keeps real power.

title: Hurricane Mitch
description: Hurricane Mitch stalls over Honduras, kills some seven thousand people and sets the economy back a generation.

title: Coup d'état
description: The army seizes President Manuel Zelaya and flies him out of the country, the first successful coup in Latin America in a generation.
